name: Cone photoreceptor synaptic glutamate output
summary: Cone photoreceptors continuously release glutamate in darkness; light-evoked hyperpolarization reduces that release. This is a downstream neural encoding stage rather than an optical-frequency oscillation.

axis.notes: Graded synaptic output after phototransduction; no single carrier frequency is assigned.

constraints: release is modulated by photoreceptor membrane potential
temporal spectrum depends on stimulus and retinal adaptation

sources.title: Phototransduction in Rods and Cones
sources.publisher: Webvision / NCBI Bookshelf, National Library of Medicine

evidence.derivation: Webvision describes light-evoked hyperpolarization decreasing or terminating dark glutamate release. Atlas records this as a downstream graded signal and intentionally does not inherit the optical carrier frequency.
